messages:
yuan: Quick perf note from today's kernel-sweep on staging (flashmosaic / FA v3 selector). Short-chat workloads (seq<=32) show p95 token latency +18% vs baseline (stable_v2). Uploading traces and a short flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/ci/4842/artifact1 :thinking_face:
perf-bot: perf-checker: regression detected for commit c9f2a3 (>10% p95). See run 2026-03-18T09:12Z.
marie: ugh. Is this consistent across batching configs? what batch sizes were used?
jake: I ran microbenchmarks. v3 kernel has higher setup overhead for small batches (bs<=8). Also noticed KV cache insert rate jumps -> more evictions. Likely interplay between paged-attn fallback and prefetch heuristics.
yuan: exact numbers: batch=1..8 p95 +12-22%, batch>=16 roughly equal. KV hitrate dropped from 98%->87% on chat traces.
aditya: can we scope this: is it a kernel cost, or our batching/kv heuristics selecting the wrong exec path? any profiling of kernel launch times vs mem copies?
jake: traced it. Two things: extra memcpy when switching to paged paths, and a short-seq codepath in v3 that skips a small prefix-cache optimization. I pasted the hotlines:
```
# from perf trace
[0.00ms] enqueue_request
[0.12ms] kernel_launch (v3_shortseq_setup)
[0.42ms] memcpy_page_prefetch
[0.90ms] gpu_compute
```
marie: thanks. so mitigation options: revert selector to v2 for short seq, tweak prefetch, or adjust batching policy.
yuan: propose feature-flagged rollout:
1) Toggle ff: `attn.kernel_selector.mode=policy` where policy can be `seq-based` -> v2 for seq<=32, v3 otherwise.
2) Canary the selector on 2% of production traffic (low QPS teams) for 48h.
3) Watch metrics: p95_token_latency, kv_hitrate, shortseq_throughput, error_rate, and tail_mem_use. Alert if p95 > baseline+8% or kv_hitrate drops >5pt.
aditya: +1. Also add a temporary autobatch tweak: bias towards batch>=8 for chat routes while canary is on (`batch.min_target=8`). That should reduce the short-batch penalty.
nina: what about the KV eviction churn? can we increase cache size for canary to see if that changes the delta?
jake: canary config will include `kv.cache_target_fraction=0.85` (higher) and `kv.prefetch=on` for the canary. We'll roll those as part of the ff.
marie: do we need a rollback plan?
yuan: yes. Rollback: ff off for 5min if any of: p95 > baseline+12% OR kv_hitrate drops >10pt OR api_error_rate +0.1%. Quick steps in playbook: `ffctl set attn.kernel_selector=stable_v2`, `ffctl set batch.min_target=1`, `ffctl set kv.*=default`.
perf-bot: notes: canary job created -> job id: canary-4842. Monitoring dashboard: https://metrics.redwood/d/attn/4842-canary
marie: ok let's run the canary tomorrow 07:00PST. who wants the oncall for first 4 hours?
aditya: I'll take the first shift. jake you on deck for kernel debugging?
jake: yep, I'll be standby.
yuan: thanks all. I'll open a short PR with the ff defaults and the playbook snippet. I'll drop the flamegraphs and perf traces in the run.
marie: cool. keep notes in the rollout doc. :thumbsup:
